gloss: hard to come by; rare; invaluable

definitions.gloss: hard to come by; rare; invaluable; precious
definitions.explanation: Describes something that is difficult to obtain or encounter, and therefore precious or valuable. Often used to express appreciation for rare opportunities or irreplaceable people.

examples.japanese: {得難|えがた}い{経験|けいけん}だった。
examples.english: It was a rare and valuable experience.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{得難|えがた}い{人材|じんざい}だ。
こんなに{親身|しんみ}になってくれる{友人|ゆうじん}は{得難|えがた}い{存在|そんざい}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think a friend who cares about you this much is a truly rare treasure.

notes:
Formed from {得|え}る (to obtain) + ～{難|がた}い (difficult to). Carries a strong positive connotation — something rare and therefore precious.

THE ～{難|がた}い PATTERN:
The suffix ～{難|がた}い attaches to verb stems to mean "hard to do":
- {忘|わす}れ{難|がた}い: hard to forget (memorable)
- {許|ゆる}し{難|がた}い: hard to forgive (unforgivable)
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い: hard to endure (unbearable)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {得難|えがた}い{経験|けいけん}: a rare and valuable experience
- {得難|えがた}い{人材|じんざい}: invaluable talent
- {得難|えがた}い{存在|そんざい}: an irreplaceable presence
- {得難|えがた}いチャンス: a rare opportunity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {珍|めずら}しい: rare, unusual (neutral — doesn't imply value)
- {貴重|きちょう}: precious, valuable (emphasizes worth)

REGISTER:
Somewhat literary/formal. More common in writing than casual speech.
